title: Normally flat initial equations lift with maximal-ideal coefficients
statement:
Let $(T,\mathfrak M,k)$ be a nonzero commutative regular local ring, with residue field $k=T/\mathfrak M$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-residue-field]. Fix a regular system of parameters $(x_0,\ldots,x_r,y_1,\ldots,y_s)$, where $r,s\geq0$, and put $P=(x_0,\ldots,x_r)$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Let $\mathfrak a\subseteq P$ be an ideal, put $R=T/\mathfrak a$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak M/\mathfrak a$, $I=P/\mathfrak a$, $A=T/P=R/I$, and assume $G=\operatorname{gr}_I R$ is flat over $A$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Let $B=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$ with all variables of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring, def-pc-standard-graded-algebra], and identify $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T=k[X_0,\ldots,X_r,Y_1,\ldots,Y_s]$ by these parameters. Let $m\geq1$ and $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in\mathfrak a$ have finite $\mathfrak M$-orders $d_i\geq1$, satisfy $f_i\in P^{d_i}$, and have initial forms $\phi_i\in B_{d_i}$ minimally generating $\ker(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak m}R)$. Here the order of $f_i$ is $\sup\{v:f_i\in\mathfrak M^v\}$ and its initial form is its class in $\mathfrak M^{d_i}/\mathfrak M^{d_i+1}$.
For every $n\geq0$ and $u\in\mathfrak a\cap P^n\cap\mathfrak M^{n+1}$, there exist coefficients $c_i\in\mathfrak M P^{n-d_i}$ for the indices with $d_i\leq n$ such that
$$u-\sum_{d_i\leq n}c_if_i\in\mathfrak a\cap P^{n+1}.$$
An empty sum is zero and $P^0=T$. No reducedness hypothesis on $R$ is imposed.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities, J. Math. Kyoto Univ. 10 (1970), proof of Lemma 20, (20.6) and the first coefficient lifting before (20.7), p.179; normal-flat initial-ideal statement attributed there to Hironaka (1964), Chapter II, Lemma 7; read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf. Archival original WANTED; the local ILO PDF is ancestor motivation (VIII 2.3.13), not the text of this lemma. No Stacks tag states this result.

proof.text: Put $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak M/P\subset A$. By [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-generators-regular-sequence], the parameter list is regular and $A=T/P$ is regular local, hence Noetherian. Its $x$-prefix is regular: the successive injectivity conditions are unchanged and its final quotient $A$ is nonzero, as required by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. By [lem-pur-regular-sequence-graded-polynomial] this gives the specified identification $H=\operatorname{gr}_P T=A[X_0,\ldots,X_r]$. The quotient $T\to R$ induces a graded surjection $H\to G$; in degree $e$ it sends the class of $t\in P^e$ to its image modulo $I^{e+1}$. It is surjective since every element of $I^e$ lifts to $P^e$. Write $K_e=\ker(H_e\to G_e)$ and let $F_i\in K_{d_i}$ be the $P$-initial class of $f_i$.

Each $G_e$ is flat over $A$: its inclusion into $G$ and the degree projection split, so the tensor map for an injection on $G_e$ is a direct summand of the injective tensor map on $G$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map, def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] to $0\to K_e\to H_e\to G_e\to0$ and $k=A/\mathfrak n$. Thus $k\otimes_A K_e\to k\otimes_A H_e$ is injective and has image the kernel of $k\otimes_A H_e\to k\otimes_A G_e$. Here $k\otimes_A N=N/\mathfrak nN$: the mutually inverse maps send $\bar a\otimes v$ to $av\bmod\mathfrak nN$ and $\bar v$ to $1\otimes v$; changing lifts changes a multiple of $\mathfrak n$, and the tensor balancing relations check both composites. Consequently reduction embeds $K_e/\mathfrak nK_e$ in $B_e=H_e/\mathfrak nH_e$, and in particular $K_e\cap\mathfrak nH_e=\mathfrak nK_e$.

source.place: Tag 00HL (lemma-flat-tor-zero); explicit residue-field tensor identification from Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product).

proof.text: Let $C=\ker(B\to G\otimes_A k)$. The injection in Step 2 identifies $K_e/\mathfrak nK_e$ with $C_e$. By [lem-trf-normal-flat-double-initial-ideal], the tangent kernel in $k[X,Y]$ is $Ck[X,Y]$. By hypothesis that same kernel is generated by the $\phi_i\in B$. Evaluating $Y=0$ in these two ideals gives $C=(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_m)$ in $B$: elements of $C$ remain themselves, and the $\phi_i$ remain themselves. Moreover $F_i\bmod\mathfrak n=\phi_i$. Indeed write $f_i=\sum_{|\alpha|=d_i}a_\alpha x^\alpha$; its class in $H_{d_i}$ has coefficients $a_\alpha\bmod P$, whereas its degree-$d_i$ class in $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T$ has coefficients $a_\alpha\bmod\mathfrak M$. These are exactly successive reduction modulo $\mathfrak n$ under the fixed parameter identifications.

source.place: Existing normal-flat comparison node, with the explicit parameter maps of its statement; Hironaka (1970), normal-flat initial-ideal comparison used before (20.7), agent assembly.

proof.text: For every $e$, the module $H_e$ has the finite monomial basis of degree $e$. Since $A$ is Noetherian, [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] makes $K_e$ finite. Let $L_e\subseteq K_e$ be the $A$-span of the finitely many $X^\alpha F_i$ with $|\alpha|=e-d_i$ and $d_i\leq e$. Step 3 says their reductions span $C_e$: take the degree-$e$ parts in $C=(\phi_i)$. By Step 2 these are all of $K_e/\mathfrak nK_e$. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators] to $L_e\subseteq K_e$ yields $L_e=K_e$. Thus every element of $K_e$ is a sum $\sum_{d_i\leq e}h_iF_i$ with $h_i\in H_{e-d_i}$. This application is degreewise to finite modules, not to the unbounded graded sum.

Fix $n\geq0$ and $u\in\mathfrak a\cap P^n\cap\mathfrak M^{n+1}$. Expand $u=\sum_{|\alpha|=n}a_\alpha x^\alpha$; products of the generators of $P$ generate $P^n$. In degree $n$ of $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak M}T=k[X,Y]$, this is $\sum(a_\alpha\bmod\mathfrak M)X^\alpha=0$, since $u\in\mathfrak M^{n+1}$. Independence of distinct polynomial monomials gives $a_\alpha\in\mathfrak M$ for every $\alpha$. Therefore $u\in\mathfrak M P^n$, and its class $U\in H_n=P^n/P^{n+1}$ belongs to $\mathfrak nH_n$. Also $U\in K_n$ because $u\in\mathfrak a$. Step 2 now gives $U\in\mathfrak nK_n$. This argument uses the parameter identification assumed in the statement and does not assume an intersection formula for the two filtrations.

source.place: Elementary monomial coefficient calculation in the specified tangent polynomial ring; no additional intersection lemma.

proof.text: By Step 4, $K_n=\sum_{d_i\leq n}H_{n-d_i}F_i$, hence $\mathfrak nK_n=\sum_{d_i\leq n}(\mathfrak nH_{n-d_i})F_i$ by distributing finite sums and scalar products. Write $U=\sum h_iF_i$ accordingly, with every coefficient of the homogeneous polynomial $h_i$ in $\mathfrak n$. Lift these finitely many coefficients along $\mathfrak M\twoheadrightarrow\mathfrak n$ and evaluate the monomials at the $x_j$. This gives $c_i\in\mathfrak M P^{n-d_i}$ whose degree-$(n-d_i)$ $P$-class is $h_i$. Multiplication of associated-graded classes then gives $u-\sum c_if_i\in P^{n+1}$. Every summand lies in $\mathfrak a$, so the difference lies also in $\mathfrak a$. This proves the required intersection. If no $d_i\leq n$, Step 4 says $K_n=0$ and the argument gives $u\in P^{n+1}$ with the empty sum. It includes $n=0$; it never uses reducedness of $R$.

source.place: Elementary lifting of finitely many polynomial coefficients and multiplication of associated-graded classes, concluding the coefficient step before Hironaka (1970), (20.7).
